text: [excited] In one single day, a university library got eleven thousand searches...
[curious] North Carolina. Finals week. Students cramming. The library catalogue, humming along.
Normally, about a hundred people search at once.
[curious] Every search was different, and weirdly picky. A human ticks maybe six filters. These ticked twenty-five.
[dramatically] Then the screen just said: queue full. Everybody out!
[deadpan] Luckily, Finland had not suddenly become famous.
[deadpan] Unluckily, the visitors were not people.
[playfully] They were bots, scraping everything to feed A.I. models. Picture a guest at a buffet who doesn't eat.
[mischievously] He fills a truck... then sneaks back in line through a different door. Again. And again.
[sighs] The library banned millions of addresses. The bots just came back from new ones.
[confident] So now an A.I. guards the door, letting people in and keeping bots out.
[serious] And this week, libraries everywhere say it's getting worse.
[amused] Somewhere, a computer now knows more about Finnish music than Finland...
[whispers] and it has never heard a single note.
